description: The Carload Waybill Sample is a stratified sample of rail waybills collected by the US Surface Transportation Board from railroads that terminate at least 4,500 carloads a year, under the rules in 49 CFR 1244. It contains sensitive shipping and revenue information and is used in rate cases, costing systems, productivity studies and state transportation plans. Coverage is all US rail traffic of those carriers, sampled every year; new sampling strata and rates, including separate intermodal strata, apply from 1 January 2021. Access: the confidential sample is restricted to railroads, federal agencies, states, practitioners in specific proceedings and approved other users who sign a confidentiality agreement, while annual Public Use Waybill Samples (2008 to 2024 on the page read) are free text-file downloads with reference guides; an archived 2007 copy is held on Harvard Dataverse. Caveats: revenue in the freight revenue field may be masked, and the 2015 to 2018 public files had a car ownership error that revised files correct. It supports rail freight flow and corridor analysis, supply chain disruption studies and calibration of freight network models, and complements the Freight Analysis Framework and the STB rail service data catalogued here.
